title: Free Is Not Open: Price and Permission
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: A two-by-two matrix that shows price and permission are separate dials, so a free resource can be closed and a paid copy of an open resource can still be open.

educational.topic: Free versus open: price and permission are independent
learningObjectives: The learner will explain why a resource that costs nothing is not necessarily open, using the four cells of the price and permission matrix.
prerequisites: The definition of an open educational resource from [Chapter 1](../../chapters/01-foundations-of-oer/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a reference picture, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: What does this cost the user?
What may the user do with it?
commonMisconceptions: Anything free to read is open
A resource that is sold in print cannot be OER
assessmentOpportunities: A library e-book costs the reader nothing but forbids copying. Which zone is it in?
A lesson plan licensed CC BY 4.0 is posted on a teacher blog. Is it OER?
A print shop sells an open textbook at cost. Is the printed copy still OER?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz buttons
controls.description: switch between exploring the poster and answering quiz questions.

controls.name: Poster zones
controls.description: hover or press to read about that part of the poster. In quiz mode a press is your answer.

controls.name: Try Again
controls.description: repeats the quiz after the last question.
